note: Prompt-cleaning catalogue, shared by both SDKs (bundled byte-identical) and copied to the ID Side cloud. Every pattern is written in a portable subset that Python's re and JavaScript's RegExp read alike; scripts and tests in both SDKs hold it. A pattern's value is its capture group `group`; a match in which that group took no part is context that rules a value out (four numbers after a version word), and the engine skips it whole. Every boundary before a value also accepts an escape written in two characters (\n, \r, \t). A value that runs on is followed by the engine to its end (`extend`), never cut and never rejected for what follows it; a match that must be followed by something no portable expression reads in linear time names the engine's check that reads it (`followed_by`), and is no match where that check fails; findings that overlap are masked as one, under the longest. The id of a detector is what an organization's policy names and what counts are reported under: ids are added, never renamed.

normalization.note: Each code point of a text is mapped on its own: dropped if it is in `ignorable`, otherwise decomposed (NFKD), stripped of the code points in `combining`, with each code point listed in `equivalents` written as its ASCII equivalent; a code point above U+FFFF is written U+FFFD. Detectors read that shadow; custom terms, domains and keywords read it with A-Z lowered to a-z.

placeholder.note: A placeholder is [LABEL_n]. Text matching this pattern is never matched by any rule, and numbering for a label starts above the highest n already present in the request.

detectors.label: EMAIL
detectors.title: E-mail address
detectors.description: An address name@domain.tld in Latin, Greek or Cyrillic letters (punycode domains included), with whatever carries its domain on (a dash, a digit, another label) and a password glued after a colon (marie@example.com:S3cret), but not a port, punctuation, or a run holding a / (a remote or a path), nor what follows a colon and a space, except an at sign between spaces, an address spelled out, user@host:path right after git clone, git remote add or set-url, scp or rsync, and an image name such as logo@2x.png.

detectors.label: PHONE
detectors.title: Phone number
detectors.description: A French number of ten digits starting 01 to 09, in pairs separated by one or two spaces, dots, dashes or slashes (the same throughout), or written +33, 0033 or (+33), and an international number written with a leading + and 9 to 15 digits, in groups or not: whatever follows a number after a separator (a currency, a time, a street number) is not part of it, letters or digits glued to it are taken with it, and when more groups follow, the longest reading of 9 to 15 digits is taken; except round thousands (+150 000 000).

detectors.label: IP_ADDRESS
detectors.title: IP address
detectors.description: An IPv4 address (four numbers of 0 to 255) with a slash and digits after it (a prefix, or a path that starts with a number), and an IPv6 address holding a digit, its longest reading that is an address (a colon and what follows it otherwise left aside) and letters or digits glued to it; except four numbers right after version, ver., release (release- included), firmware or revision, glued to v (v1.2.3.4) or after v and a space (v 1.2.3.4, never an option -v), or followed by a fifth, and a compressed IPv6 address with neither a group of three or more hexadecimal digits nor an IPv4 tail (::1).

detectors.label: MAC_ADDRESS
detectors.title: MAC address
detectors.description: Six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by colons or by dashes (the same throughout), or three groups of four separated by dots (xxxx.xxxx.xxxx), but not without a separator nor in the shortened form 0:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e.

detectors.label: CARD
detectors.title: Payment card number
detectors.description: 13 to 19 digits of a known card network passing the Luhn check, written together or grouped 4-4-4-4, 4-4-4-4-3, 4-6-5 or 4-6-4 with one or two spaces, dashes or dots (the same throughout).

detectors.label: IBAN
detectors.title: IBAN
detectors.description: An IBAN of its country's registered length passing the mod-97 check, written together or in groups of four counted from the check digits or from the country, separated by spaces or dashes (a dash or two spaces after the country included), but not a French RIB grouped as bank, branch, account and key.

detectors.label: BIC
detectors.title: BIC / SWIFT code
detectors.description: An 8- or 11-character code in capitals, written together or spaced 4-2-2-3 (letters or digits glued to a spaced one taken with it, a word after it left aside), with a valid country code, only within 64 characters of the word BIC (or B.I.C.) or SWIFT.

detectors.label: NIR
detectors.title: French social security number (NIR)
detectors.description: 15 characters (Corsica 2A and 2B included) passing the key check, written together or grouped by spaces, dots or dashes.

detectors.label: SIREN
detectors.title: SIREN number
detectors.description: 9 digits passing the Luhn check, grouped or not by spaces, dots or dashes, only within 64 characters of the word SIREN, SIRENE or RCS (or R.C.S.).

detectors.label: SIRET
detectors.title: SIRET number
detectors.description: 14 digits passing the Luhn check (or the La Poste rule), grouped 3-3-3-5, 3-3-3-3-2 or not at all, only within 64 characters of the word SIRET (or S.I.R.E.T.).

detectors.label: VAT_NUMBER
detectors.title: French VAT number
detectors.description: FR followed by a two-character key and a SIREN, spaces, dots or dashes allowed between the parts, passing the key check.

detectors.label: PLATE
detectors.title: French licence plate
detectors.description: A plate of the current AA-123-AA format in capitals, with dashes, spaces, dots or nothing between the parts and an optional department (-69, -2A), but not the pre-2009 format, a lowercase plate or 000.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: OpenAI API key
detectors.description: A key starting sk-, sk-proj-, sk-svcacct- or sk-admin- followed by at least 40 characters, taken to the end of the token however long, URL escapes such as %2F included.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: Anthropic API key
detectors.description: A key starting sk-ant- followed by at least 32 characters, taken to the end of the token however long, URL escapes such as %2F included.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: Google API key
detectors.description: A key starting AIza followed by 35 characters (Gemini and other Google APIs).

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: Mistral API key
detectors.description: 32 letters and digits within 64 characters of the word Mistral, MistralAI, MistralClient or Codestral, since the key has no prefix of its own.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: DeepSeek API key
detectors.description: sk- followed by exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: ID Side secret key
detectors.description: sk_live_ or sk_test_ followed by exactly 32 letters and digits, the format of this SDK's keys.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: AWS access key id
detectors.description: An access key id starting AKIA, ASIA or another AWS key id prefix followed by 16 capitals and digits, but not the 40-character secret access key, which has no prefix.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: GitHub token
detectors.description: A token starting ghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_ or ghr_ followed by at least 36 characters, or github_pat_ followed by at least 22, taken to the end of the token however long, URL escapes such as %2F included.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: GitLab token
detectors.description: A token with a documented GitLab prefix (glpat-, gldt-, glrt-, glcbt-, glptt-, glft-, glffct-, glimt-, glagent-, glsoat-, gloas-, glwt-) followed by at least 20 characters, taken to the end of the token however long, URL escapes such as %2F included, any suffix attached to it by dots included.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: Slack token or webhook
detectors.description: A token starting xoxa-, xoxb-, xoxc-, xoxd-, xoxe-, xoxo-, xoxp-, xoxr-, xoxs- or xapp- (rotating app-level tokens included) followed by at least 10 characters, and a hooks.slack.com webhook URL with or without its scheme, each taken to its end however long, URL escapes such as %2F included (one in the first ten characters too).

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: Stripe secret key
detectors.description: A secret starting sk_live_, sk_test_, rk_live_ or rk_test_ followed by at least 20 characters, or whsec_ followed by at least 24, taken to the end of the token however long, URL escapes such as %2F included (publishable pk_ keys are public by design), an sk_ key of exactly 32 characters after its prefix being counted as an ID Side key.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: Twilio API key
detectors.description: SK followed by 32 hexadecimal characters.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: SendGrid API key
detectors.description: SG. followed by two parts of 22 and 43 characters.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: npm token
detectors.description: npm_ followed by 36 letters and digits.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: PyPI token
detectors.description: A pypi- upload token for pypi.org or test.pypi.org, taken to the end of the token however long, URL escapes such as %2F included.

detectors.label: API_KEY
detectors.title: Azure key
detectors.description: The AccountKey= (88 characters) or SharedAccessKey= (44 characters) value of a connection string, with any base64 characters glued to it and URL escapes such as %2B included, spaces allowed around =, and 32 hexadecimal characters, in lower or upper case, within 64 characters of the word Azure.

detectors.label: TOKEN
detectors.title: JSON Web Token
detectors.description: Three base64url parts separated by dots, the first starting eyJ, and any further dotted part (an encrypted token has five), a part longer than 8,192 characters included, taken to the end of the token however long, URL escapes such as %2F included, without the full stop or other punctuation that follows it.

detectors.label: TOKEN
detectors.title: Authorization header value
detectors.description: The credential after Authorization: Bearer or Proxy-Authorization: Bearer (in a header, JSON or code) whatever its length, after Bearer elsewhere when it has 16 characters or more and holds a digit or a punctuation mark, and after Authorization: Basic (8 characters or more), each taken to the end of the token however long, URL escapes such as %2F included.

detectors.label: PRIVATE_KEY
detectors.title: Private key
detectors.description: A PEM, OpenSSH or PGP private key block from its BEGIN line to its END line however its lines are written (within 65,536 characters); without its END line (or past that), when key material comes right after the BEGIN line (32 base64 characters in one or two runs, the first of 16 or more, with nothing before them but blanks, line breaks real or escaped, line prefixes, quotes, placeholders and PEM or PGP header lines), everything from the BEGIN line to the end of the text, placeholders and later BEGIN lines included. A BEGIN line with no key material right after it is quoted, not a key: left as it is under Mask, it blocks under Block.

detectors.label: PASSWORD
detectors.title: Password in a connection string
detectors.description: The user and password before the last @ of a database or messaging URL (postgres, mysql, mongodb, redis, amqp...) or of an Oracle thin URL, whatever follows the host, the quoted or unquoted value of Password= or Pwd= within 64 characters of a word such as Server, Host or Database, and the value of PGPASSWORD, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, MYSQL_PASSWORD and their kin or of spring.datasource.password, each taken to its delimiter however long, unless that value is a lookup of the environment (os.environ, os.getenv, process.env) or a reference to a variable in braces (${NAME}), in a URL too; a password whose first 256 characters hold neither @ nor its end is not read.

detectors.label: CREDENTIALS
detectors.title: Credentials in a URL
detectors.description: The user and password (or a token) before the last @ of any other URL with a scheme, such as an https:// address, or after // without a scheme when a password follows the user (//user:password@host), whatever follows the host, except the user git alone (ssh://git@host) and a password or token that is a reference to a variable in braces (${NAME}); a user or a password whose first 256 characters hold neither @ nor its end is not read.

detectors.label: SECRET
detectors.title: Generic secret assignment
detectors.description: A value of 6 characters or more, taken whole to its delimiter however long (a blank, a comma, a semicolon, or the closing quote, escapes included), quoted or not, assigned either to a name one of whose words is password, passwd, passphrase, pwd, pass, secret, token, credential(s), mdp, api_key or access_key, words joined by _, . or - and at most three on either side (db_password, auth.token, x-api-key, but not dbPass or mypassword), or to mot de passe, the default of a lookup of the environment included there (os.getenv("NAME", "..."), process.env.NAME || "..."), or to one to three capitalised words followed by _KEY (STRIPE_KEY); except a type name, true, false, null or the lookup itself; off by default, since it also finds values that are not secrets.
